In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a non-invasive, long-term, semi intracellular electropysiological monitoring system.

the establishment of an IN-CELL recording approach for long term, semi intracellular, electrophysiological recordings of APs and subthreshold synaptic potentials from neurons in culture, in vivo, and in situ.
the development of a new non-invasive approach for the long-term monitoring of neuronal activity, which can be applied to a variety of cell types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of the ultrastructural neuron-gMμEs configuration in hippocampal neurons, is the first step towards the generation of IN-CELL configuration.
the necessary morphologic and ultrastructural relationships for generating the IN-CELL recordings are formed between hippocampus cells and the gMEs.

the gMμES can be engulfed by hippocampal cells, and the necessary morphological relationships to generate the "IN-CELL recording" configuration are formed between them, and that the IN-CELL recordings of spontaneous electrical activity from cultured hippocampal cells are most probably generated by cells that engulf gM μES
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IN-CELL recordings configuration, which is based on a non-invasive extracellular multi-electrode array (MEA), can be used to record from cultured neurons of vertebrate origin.

the gMμEmicroelectrodes, which were designed for extracellular recordings, are able to generate the INCELL recording configuration, which provides attenuated intracellular recordings of APs, and synaptic potentials.
a non-invasive extracellular MEA system can be converted to an IN-CELL recording system, by which neurons engulf gold mushroom-shaped micro-electrodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IN-CELL recordings are a promising approach to study electrical properties of cultured neurons and their synapses.
the IN-CELL system provides a novel non-invasive approach to study the electrical properties of neurons and their synaptic connections.
the gMμEmEA system can be used to record from cultured hippocampal cells in the IN-CELL mode.
